unit: code: 0 fine, 1 among about the widest 25% of ranges (a ranking, widest share range at or above 0.52; a fixed 0.4 limit would flag 60% of cells), 2 features outside the range seen at survey clusters, 3 both
method: Split conformal prediction on spatial (leave-districts-out) out-of-fold errors of the share model, 4 bins by predicted value, target coverage 80%. Range = prediction +/- bin half-width, clipped to 0..1. Grid, solar and unserved are bounded separately, so the three ranges do not sum to 1.
coverage_check: Nested spatial coverage: grid 80%, solar 80%, unserved 80%
labels: Nigeria DHS 2023-24 (DHS-8), restricted data. Only model-derived outputs are published.
feature_sources: population: WorldPop/GP/100m/pop (2020) [CC BY 4.0]; built_up_surface: JRC/GHSL/P2023A/GHS_BUILT_S (2020) [CC BY 4.0]; night_lights_bm: NASA/VIIRS/002/VNP46A2 (Black Marble) median 2024-01-01 to 2026-01-01 [NASA open data, cite Black Marble (confirm)]; travel_time_city: projects/malariaatlasproject/assets/accessibility/accessibility_to_cities/2015_v1_0 [CC BY 4.0]; travel_time_health: projects/malariaatlasproject/assets/accessibility/accessibility_to_healthcare/2019 [CC BY 4.0]; slope: USGS/SRTMGL1_003 (ee.Terrain.slope on 100 m mean elevation) [Public domain]; elevation: USGS/SRTMGL1_003 [Public domain]
limitations: Modelled estimate from 1380 survey clusters, not a census. Training label is the MAIN lighting source (DHS hv262), so households using grid plus solar count as grid. DHS cluster locations are displaced by up to 2 km (urban) and 5 km (rural). Solar versus unserved is separated less well than grid versus non-grid. Night lights and satellite layers cannot see small solar systems. Unserved here means no electricity and no solar as the main light source (mostly torch and fuel lighting), not the official access gap. Households with electricity whose main light is a torch (power cuts) are counted as grid, so the grid share mixes grid access with grid supply (flag share_grid_unreliable). National shares from the map are about 6 points lower on grid and 6 higher on unserved than the survey, mostly because the map weights cells by people and the survey weights households (urban households are smaller, and WorldPop puts fewer people in urban cells than the survey sample does). Quote rankings, not national levels. The range is calibrated on cluster-level errors, which include household sampling noise (about 25 households per cluster) and GPS displacement, so it is wider than the uncertainty of the true cell share. Coverage holds on average across districts, not for every cell.
title: Do-not-trust mask, 1 km
